key_insight: The paper develops dynamic RANS closures from temporally filtered Navier–Stokes equations, extending a dynamic k-ω model that adapts its eddy-viscosity coefficient and remains robust under temporal coarsening.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more reliable coarse-grained turbulence model for engineering flows where transition, separation, and reattachment must be predicted under limited resolution.
method: Derive dynamic RANS closures from the exact relations of temporally filtered Navier–Stokes equations.
Extend the framework to a k-ω formulation with an alternative treatment to avoid non-physical free-stream turbulence decay.
Validate the model on scale-resolving simulations under coarsened temporal sampling.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a simulation campaign showing the dynamic k-ω model remains robust to temporal coarsening and captures laminar-to-turbulent transition plus boundary-layer separation/reattachment sensitivity to free-stream turbulence.
watch_item: The approach still depends on dynamically computed coefficients and careful boundary-condition treatment, so stability and calibration may be case-dependent in practical deployments.
paper_title: Development of a class of dynamic RANS closures for coarse-grained approaches to turbulence
